# Outline -- The Ashen Pact

_Novel Template (Fiction / Fantasy). Replace every `_italic_` example with your own ideas. Delete any section that doesn't serve the story you're writing._

---

## Front Matter

- **Working Title:** _e.g. The Ashen Pact_
- **Series:** _e.g. The Ember Throne Saga, Book 2 -- or leave blank for standalone_
- **Genre:** _e.g. Epic Fantasy with political intrigue_
- **Tone:** _e.g. Grimdark, slow burn, morally grey_
- **POV / Tense:** _e.g. Third-person limited, past tense, two alternating POVs_
- **Target Length:** _e.g. 90,000 words / ~30 chapters_
- **Logline:** _One sentence. Who wants what, and what's in their way?_
  _e.g. A disgraced necromancer must resurrect the king he once betrayed before the dead empress claims the throne._
- **Premise:** _Two or three sentences expanding the logline into the hook._
- **Theme:** _What the story is really about beneath the plot._
  _e.g. Loyalty vs. self-preservation. Whether the dead owe anything to the living._

---

## Worldbuilding Hooks

_Just the bones here. Deep worldbuilding lives in profiles/lore and profiles/locations. This section is for the three or four facts the reader needs to understand the story._

- **Setting Summary:** _Where and when does this story take place?_
- **Magic / Tech Rules:** _What are the limits? What's the cost?_
- **Central Conflict of the World:** _What tension exists before the protagonist enters the story?_

---

## Character Anchors

_One line per character here. Full profiles live in profiles/characters and are built using the Profile Builder. The point of this section is to list the load-bearing cast at a glance._

- **Protagonist:** _Name -- the want, the flaw, the lie they believe._
- **Antagonist:** _Name -- what they want, and why they believe it's right._
- **Ally / Mentor:** _Name -- what they teach the protagonist._
- **Foil / Rival:** _Name -- which trait of the protagonist they reflect or contrast._
- **Supporting Cast:** _Brief list._

---

## Act I -- Setup (roughly 25%)

_The ordinary world, the inciting incident, and the decision to act._

- **Opening Image:** _What does the reader see first? What mood does it set?_
- **Protagonist's Status Quo:** _Life before the story starts. What do they want? What do they lack?_
- **Inciting Incident:** _The event that disturbs the status quo and makes the story necessary. Usually lands in chapter 1-3._
- **Debate / Refusal:** _The protagonist resists the call. Why? What are they afraid of?_
- **Threshold / Break into Act II:** _The point of no return. The protagonist commits to the journey and can no longer go back._

---

## Act II -- Confrontation (roughly 50%)

_The longest act. Escalating complications, a midpoint reversal, and a crushing low point._

- **First Trials:** _Early obstacles. The protagonist is reacting more than leading._
- **B-Story / Subplot:** _The secondary thread that runs parallel (romance, mentor relationship, internal growth). Should speak to the theme._
- **Midpoint:** _Stakes are raised. New information reframes the problem. Often a false victory or false defeat._
- **Escalation:** _The antagonist counters. Complications multiply. Allies fall away or reveal themselves._
- **All Is Lost / Dark Night of the Soul:** _The crushing low point. The protagonist's plan fails. They must change internally to move forward._

---

## Act III -- Resolution (roughly 25%)

_The protagonist applies their internal change to solve the external problem._

- **Break into Act III:** _The new plan. The protagonist commits with new understanding._
- **Climax:** _The final confrontation. The external conflict and the internal conflict resolve in the same beat._
- **Resolution / Falling Action:** _The new normal. What has changed? What lingers?_
- **Closing Image:** _Mirror or contrast of the opening image. Shows the transformation._

---

## Chapter-by-Chapter Plan

_Rough one-to-two-line summaries per chapter. Update as you draft. Not every chapter needs to be planned before writing -- some writers plan all, others only the next three._

- **Chapter 1:** _e.g. Kael returns to the ruined capital and finds the king's signet ring on a corpse that isn't the king's. (Inciting incident.)_
- **Chapter 2:** _..._
- **Chapter 3:** _..._
